entries.section_heading: Better seed systems begin with better questions.
entries.text: Better seed systems begin with better questions. Sage Harvest Agro Pvt. Limited is an independent, practitioner-led advisory firm focused on seed supply chain strategy, transformation and practical decision support. WHY WE EXIST

entries.section_heading: Bridging field realities with management decisions.
entries.text: Bridging field realities with management decisions. Seed businesses operate across biological uncertainty, seasonal cycles, quality constraints, infrastructure decisions, working capital and market commitments. A good strategy must connect these pieces rather than optimize them in isolation. Our approach combines operating experience with analytics, digital tools and sustainability thinking to help leadership teams see the system clearly and act on the highest-value constraints. OUR PURPOSE & DIRECTION

entries.section_heading: Stronger seed systems. Better decisions. Lasting value.
entries.text: Stronger seed systems. Better decisions. Lasting value. We exist to help seed and agri-businesses build supply chains that are more resilient, data-informed and ready for the realities of the field. OUR PURPOSE
Make complexity actionable. Connect field realities, operational performance and leadership priorities so businesses can make clearer decisions and turn insight into practical action. OUR VISION

entries.section_heading: A stronger, more resilient seed ecosystem.
entries.text: A stronger, more resilient seed ecosystem. A seed sector where sound planning, dependable quality, responsible resource use and effective supply chains help businesses and farmers thrive. OUR MISSION

Bring strategy closer to execution. Provide independent, practitioner-led advisory that combines deep industry experience, analytics and digital thinking with recommendations grounded in operational reality. WHAT WE WORK TOWARDS 01 Resilience — anticipate risk and strengthen supply continuity. 02 Performance — improve planning, quality, service and working-capital decisions. 03 Intelligence — make better use of data, analytics and digital tools. 04 Responsible growth — integrate sustainability and long-term value into business choices. 01
Industry depth Practical understanding of seed production, processing, quality, storage, inventory and distribution. 02
Transformation From process redesign to digital decision systems, we focus on changes that can work in the operating environment. 03
Independent perspective Objective advisory support for leaders evaluating priorities, investments, risks and transformation choices. HOW WE ENGAGE

Independent thinking. Practical next steps. Each engagement starts with the business decision, the operating context and the evidence available. The work is shaped around the client's priorities—from a focused diagnostic to a transformation roadmap—so recommendations are relevant, testable and grounded in execution. Explore our advisory areas →

entries.page_title: Seed Production Carbon Potential Calculator | Sage Harvest Labs
entries.text: Developer & Disclosures Developed by Raja Vadlamani This is an independent public scenario tool developed by Raja Vadlamani to help companies explore the potential climate and carbon implications of improved practices across seed-production landscapes. Purpose: education, screening and scenario exploration. It is not intended to establish a company's official GHG inventory, carbon footprint, regulatory compliance position or carbon-credit entitlement. Full disclosure: This calculator is an analytical and educational scenario tool. It is not a carbon-credit registry, certification system, validation/verification service, legal opinion, accounting opinion, investment recommendation, tax advice, or assurance statement. Results are estimates generated from user inputs and illustrative assumptions. They must not be represented as verified emission reductions, issued Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs), offsets, removals, Scope 1/2/3 inventory results, or guaranteed financial value. Methodology disclosure: The calculator does not substitute for an approved methodology, project design document, baseline study, monitoring plan, additionality assessment, uncertainty assessment, leakage assessment, permanence assessment where applicable, validation, verification or registry decision. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) currently lists BM AG04.002 — Emission reduction through improved management practices in rice cultivation under the CCTS Offset Mechanism. Reference: BEE, “Methodologies and Tools under Offset Mechanism”, last updated 7 July 2026. Credit disclosure: A modeled tCO₂e reduction is not automatically a carbon credit. Under the CCTS Offset Mechanism, project registration and issuance are subject to applicable eligibility, methodology, monitoring and validation/verification requirements. This tool does not predict or guarantee issuance. Reference: BEE CCTS Offset Mechanism materials and approved methodologies. Baseline & factor disclosure: The baseline practice share and eligible-area share are screening inputs; actual baseline, additionality, leakage, uncertainty and buffer treatment must follow the applicable methodology. This teaser applies no generic credit haircut. The crop-level reduction factors in this tool are illustrative screening placeholders for scenario analysis. They are not claimed to be official BEE/CCTS factors. For an actual project, replace them with methodology-specific equations, parameters, activity data and project/baseline calculations supported by appropriate evidence. Ownership & claim-rights disclosure: In contract-grower seed production, the right to claim, transfer or sell reductions depends on contractual arrangements, the applicable accounting/crediting framework and programme rules. A reduction should not be counted twice across incompatible claims. This tool does not assess ownership, claim-rights or double-counting for any specific project. GHG accounting disclosure: This calculator is not a GHG Protocol inventory calculator. The GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard provides requirements and guidance for accounting and reporting land-sector emissions and removals; its effective date is 1 January 2027. Any corporate reporting claim should be assessed against the applicable GHG Protocol requirements and the company's defined inventory boundary. Reference: GHG Protocol, Land Sector and Removals Standard v1.1 and Guidance, 2026. Scope disclosure: This calculator does not determine whether a company's reductions can be counted toward a corporate GHG inventory, Scope 3 category, product carbon footprint, insetting claim or any other corporate climate claim. Such treatment depends on the relevant accounting framework, boundary, ownership/control rules and claim requirements. No guarantee: Actual carbon-reduction outcomes, credit volumes, eligibility, verification results, issuance, marketability or economic value may differ materially from this scenario output. Public reference sources: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) — Methodologies and Tools under Offset Mechanism ; GHG Protocol — Land Sector and Removals Standard ; GHG Protocol — Land Sector and Removals Guidance . Users should consult the latest official publications before relying on any result for a real project. Data privacy: No data is uploaded or stored by this calculator. Inputs and calculations remain in your browser while you use this standalone page. The CCTS framework and approved methodologies can change. Users should check the latest BEE/Indian Carbon Market documents and obtain appropriate technical, legal, accounting and carbon-market advice before relying on the results for a real project. Seed Production Carbon Potential Calculator v1.8.1 • Area conversion: 1 acre = 0.404685642 ha • Results are annualized model outputs. Carbon-credit issuance is subject to the applicable programme, methodology, project eligibility, baseline, additionality, monitoring, validation/verification and registry decisions.

entries.section_heading: Cotton Hybrid Quality Risk: Using Lot-Level Data to Find the Signal
entries.text: Cotton Hybrid Quality Risk: Using Lot-Level Data to Find the Signal An anonymised example of how seed-quality data can move a discussion from anecdotal concern to evidence-based risk assessment. Challenge Determine whether quality failures are disproportionately concentrated in one production or genetic segment of a cotton hybrid portfolio compared with a relevant comparator. Approach Compare lot-level outcomes and apply appropriate statistical tests—including a Chi-square test and a two-proportion comparison—to assess whether the observed difference is likely to be meaningful rather than random variation. Management implication Lot-level evidence can help management focus root-cause investigation, sampling and corrective action where risk is concentrated rather than treating all lots as equally exposed. GREENFIELD PROJECTS

Greenfield Seed Infrastructure & Operating Models Experience in developing greenfield concepts for seed processing, storage and supply-chain infrastructure, translating business requirements into practical operating models. Typical lens Capacity planning, site and infrastructure requirements, process design, technology and equipment evaluation, storage strategy, implementation sequencing and operating readiness. Related capability → FORECASTING & PLANNING

Demand Forecasting & Supply Chain Planning Applying regression and machine-learning approaches to improve demand forecasting, production planning and supply-chain decision support. Typical lens Historical demand, geography, product or hybrid characteristics, seasonality and contextual variables; model comparison, forecast evaluation and scenario-based planning. Related capability → DATA & DIGITAL ARCHITECTURE

Supply Chain Data Architecture Designing the data foundations required to connect operational information, analytics and management decisions across complex supply-chain environments. Typical lens Data sources, feature structures, integration layers, data quality, traceability, analytics workflows and decision-support architecture. Related capability → SATELLITE INTELLIGENCE

Satellite Data Acquisition & Interpretation Using satellite-derived information as a scalable source of field intelligence for seed production, crop monitoring, risk assessment and planning. Typical lens Data-source selection, acquisition methods, spatial and temporal resolution, preprocessing, field-level interpretation, vegetation indicators, weather context and translation of imagery into operational decisions. Related capability → CLIMATE & SUSTAINABILITY

Climate Assessment & Decision Tools Developing practical approaches to assess climate exposure, resource efficiency and sustainability opportunities within agricultural supply chains. Typical lens Climate variables, field and supply-chain activity data, emissions and resource indicators, scenario assessment, MRV considerations and decision-support tools. Related capability → RISK & ASSURANCE

Supply-Chain Due Diligence Assessing operational capability, controls, infrastructure, traceability and risk in support of management and transaction decisions. Typical lens Operational readiness, physical assets, process controls, data integrity and execution risk. Related capability → GLOBAL TRADE

Cross-Border Market Facilitation Supporting market-entry thinking, partner evaluation and commercial discussions for seed and agri-businesses exploring international opportunities. Typical lens Market fit, partner capability, commercial terms, regulatory considerations and execution planning. Related capability → TRACEABILITY

Digital Supply-Chain Visibility Mapping information flows from production through processing and market to identify gaps in reconciliation, traceability and operational control. Typical lens Data capture, traceability, reconciliation, integration points and exception management. Related capability → A NOTE ON CONFIDENTIALITY

Real experience. Responsible storytelling. Client-specific assignments and confidential operational data are not disclosed. Public case perspectives focus on the challenge, methodology and lessons without identifying confidential clients or commercially sensitive information.
Confidentiality Principles. Sage Harvest recognises that advisory work can involve commercially sensitive information, strategic decisions and operating data. Last updated: 6 October 2026

Our approach Information shared with Sage Harvest in connection with a potential or confirmed engagement is handled with appropriate discretion and care. Information is used for the purpose for which it has been provided or as otherwise agreed. Access is limited, where reasonably practicable, to people or service providers who need the information for the relevant purpose. Confidential information is not intentionally disclosed to third parties except where authorised, required by law, or necessary for agreed professional or service-provider purposes. Appropriate safeguards are used for documents and information under our control. Confidentiality expectations may continue after completion of an engagement, subject to applicable law and the terms agreed with the client.

Initial enquiries An initial enquiry through the Sage Harvest website or by email does not, by itself, establish a formal client relationship or a comprehensive confidentiality obligation. Please do not send commercially sensitive, confidential or restricted information in an initial enquiry. A brief description of the challenge is normally sufficient for an initial conversation.

Engagement-specific terms Where an assignment involves material confidential information, Sage Harvest may recommend an appropriate confidentiality agreement or include confidentiality provisions in the engagement documentation. The confidentiality obligations applicable to a particular assignment will be governed by the relevant engagement letter, NDA or other written terms agreed with the client.

Puja Puja is an AI-assisted voice guide for exploring public Sage Harvest information. It is not an appropriate channel for confidential or commercially sensitive information. Please do not submit such information to Puja.
Contact For questions about confidentiality, contact Raja Vadlamani , Sage Harvest Agro Pvt. Limited.

entries.section_heading: From data ingestion to adaptive action.
entries.text: From data ingestion to adaptive action. Sage Harvest explores practical applications of AI, analytics, satellite imagery, weather intelligence, traceability and decision-support systems across the seed supply chain. We start with the decision that needs to improve, identify the data required, test the analytical approach and then design the workflow around how people actually operate. 01

Predictive Analytics Use historical and operational data to estimate production, demand, risk and other business outcomes. Yield and production forecasting Demand and inventory intelligence Risk scoring and early-warning indicators Scenario and sensitivity analysis 02

Satellite & Weather Intelligence Bring external environmental signals into planning where they can improve visibility without creating unnecessary field-level technology complexity. Satellite-derived crop indicators Weather and climate signals Geographic risk assessment Production monitoring 03

Conversational Decision Support Explore natural-language interfaces that allow supply-chain teams to interrogate scenarios, assumptions and operational choices. Planning questions in plain language Scenario comparison Goal-state and action recommendations Human-in-the-loop decision workflows 04

Digital Traceability Connect production, processing, quality and movement data to create a more transparent seed chain. Lot and batch traceability Data-flow and integration design Reconciliation and exception management Decision-ready operational dashboards 05

AI-Enabled Supply Chain Transformation Move from isolated pilots to practical operating models where analytics becomes part of recurring management decisions. Use-case prioritization Data readiness assessment Proof-of-concept design Adoption and governance roadmap 06

Responsible AI & Validation AI recommendations are useful only when their assumptions, data quality and performance can be understood and tested. Data-quality assessment Model validation and monitoring Human review and escalation Performance measurement OUR APPROACH

Data → Insight → Decision → Action → Learning. The objective is not to add AI for its own sake. It is to improve the quality, speed and consistency of decisions across the seed supply chain. Discuss a digital or AI opportunity

Raja Vadlamani From seed to supply chain to strategy — bringing nearly four decades of experience across the seed and agri-business ecosystem to the next chapter of industry transformation. Practitioner-led. Independent. Seed-industry focused. THE PRACTITIONER BEHIND SAGE HARVEST

Deep operating experience. Future-facing thinking. Raja Vadlamani is a senior seed and supply-chain professional whose career has spanned nearly four decades across the seed and agri-business industry. His experience covers supply-chain leadership, seed production, processing, quality, warehousing, inventory, transformation and strategic initiatives. His professional journey includes experience with Corteva, Advanta, Shriram Bioseed and SeedWorks International , giving Sage Harvest a perspective shaped by different organizations, operating models and stages of industry evolution. At Sage Harvest, this experience is translated into independent advisory work—helping organizations strengthen supply chains, use data and AI more effectively, build climate resilience, evaluate transactions and pursue international opportunities. Privacy Policy. This notice explains how Sage Harvest Agro Pvt. Limited handles personal information in connection with this website and its visitor-facing services. Last updated: 6 October 2026
1. Who we are Sage Harvest Agro Pvt. Limited (“Sage Harvest”, “we”, “us” or “our”) operates this website and provides independent advisory services in seed and agri-business supply chains.

2. Information we may receive We may receive information that you choose to provide when you contact us, such as your name, email address, organisation, role and the information contained in your enquiry. When you use Puja, our AI-assisted voice guide, the service may process the text or audio you submit, together with technical information needed to establish and operate the voice session. The current website does not contain a conventional contact form or an installed analytics script.

3. How we use information Information may be used to respond to enquiries, discuss potential engagements, provide and operate Puja, maintain website functionality, protect the website and services, and comply with applicable legal obligations.

4. Puja and third-party services Puja uses a Sage Harvest-controlled Cloudflare Worker to obtain a short-lived access token and then connects to Google's Gemini Live service for the AI-assisted voice interaction. The website does not expose a Gemini API key in its client-side code. Because Puja relies on third-party infrastructure, information transmitted through the service may also be subject to the relevant provider terms and privacy practices. Sage Harvest does not represent that third-party processing is governed solely by this policy.

5. Website hosting and technical information The website is published using Cloudflare Pages, with source code maintained in a GitHub repository. Cloudflare may process technical information, including IP addresses and request data, to deliver, secure and operate the website under its own privacy and security practices. GitHub may process information associated with repository access and development services under its own policies.

6. Cookies and analytics The current Sage Harvest website does not intentionally deploy its own analytics or advertising cookies. Third-party services linked from the website, including YouTube, LinkedIn or other external destinations, operate under their own privacy practices when you visit or interact with those services.

7. Sharing and disclosure We do not sell personal information. Information may be shared with service providers where reasonably necessary to operate the website or an engagement, where you have requested or authorised the disclosure, or where disclosure is required or permitted by law.

8. Retention We seek to retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, for legitimate business needs, or as required by applicable law. Specific retention periods may depend on the nature of an enquiry or engagement.

9. Your choices and requests If you have a question about personal information held by Sage Harvest, or wish to request access, correction, deletion or other action available under applicable law, please contact us at raja.vadlamani@gmail.com . We may need to verify your identity before acting on a request.

10. Data protection framework Sage Harvest intends to handle personal information in accordance with applicable data-protection requirements and evolving regulatory obligations, including India's Digital Personal Data Protection framework as applicable to the organisation and the relevant processing activity. This notice is not a representation that every provision of that framework is currently in force or applicable to every visitor.
11. Changes to this policy We may update this notice when our website, services or legal obligations change. The latest version will be published on this page with its update date.
12. Contact For privacy questions or requests, contact Raja Vadlamani , Sage Harvest Agro Pvt. Limited.

entries.section_heading: Sustainability should be designed into the supply chain.
entries.text: Sustainability should be designed into the supply chain. Climate variability, water availability, energy use, production practices, logistics and infrastructure increasingly affect both the economics and resilience of seed businesses. Sage Harvest helps organizations translate sustainability ambitions into practical operating priorities, measurement frameworks and improvement programs. Where carbon accounting, MRV or market mechanisms are involved, approaches must be aligned with applicable methodologies, standards and independent validation. 01

Climate-Smart Supply Chains Identify operational interventions that strengthen resilience while improving resource and cost efficiency. Climate-risk assessment Supply-chain vulnerability mapping Climate-smart operating practices Resilience and adaptation roadmaps 02

Resource Efficiency Examine water, energy, processing, storage and logistics choices through both economic and environmental lenses. Water-use efficiency Energy and process efficiency Storage and logistics optimization Resource-performance indicators 03

Carbon & MRV Advisory Build practical measurement, reporting and verification approaches for relevant agricultural and supply-chain interventions. Activity and emissions mapping MRV framework design Data and evidence architecture Methodology and validation readiness 04

Regenerative & Low-Emission Production Evaluate production practices that may improve soil, water, resource efficiency and emissions performance while protecting seed quality and yield objectives. Climate-smart production assessment Water-management interventions Low-emission practice evaluation Field-to-supply-chain measurement 05

Sustainability Audits Independent reviews of supply-chain sustainability practices, controls, evidence and improvement opportunities. Supply-chain sustainability audits ESG process and control reviews Data and documentation assessment Corrective-action roadmaps 06

Carbon Opportunity Assessment Assess where credible carbon or environmental-value opportunities may exist and what evidence and operating changes would be required. Opportunity screening Baseline and activity-data review MRV readiness assessment Commercial and implementation considerations OUR BELIEF

entries.section_heading: Sustainability becomes powerful when it improves both resilience and economics.
entries.text: Sustainability becomes powerful when it improves both resilience and economics. The objective is not sustainability reporting for its own sake.
